# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 14 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 14 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_014_page_001.jpg

---

14:1 Again, one preparing to sail and about to travel through savage waves cries out to wood more fragile than the vessel carrying him.

14:2 For that vessel was devised by a longing for gain, and wisdom was the craftsman who built it.

14:3 But your providence, O Father, pilots it, because you have given even in the sea a path, and among the waves a safe way,

14:4 showing that you are able to save out of every danger, so that even one who lacks experience may embark.

14:5 And it is your will that the works of your wisdom should not be idle; therefore people also entrust their lives to the smallest piece of wood, and passing through the surge on a raft, they come through safely.

14:6 For in the beginning also, when arrogant giants were perishing, the hope of the world took refuge on a raft, and guided by your hand left to the age a seed of generations.

14:7 For blessed is wood through which righteousness comes.

14:8 But the handmade idol is accursed, both it and the one who made it — he because he made it, and it because it was called a god though it is perishable.

14:9 For equally hateful to God are both the ungodly and his ungodliness,

14:10 and both the thing done and the one who did it will be punished together.

14:11 Therefore also upon the idols of the nations there will be a visitation, because in the creation of God they became an abomination, a stumbling block to the souls of men, and a snare to the feet of the foolish.

14:12 For the devising of idols was the beginning of spiritual fornication, and the invention of them was the corruption of life.

14:13 For neither were they from the beginning, nor will they be forever.

14:14 For by the empty boasting of men they entered into the world, and therefore a speedy end was devised for them.

14:15 For a father, afflicted with grief at an untimely bereavement, made an image of the child taken away so quickly, and henceforth honored as a god what was then a dead human being, and handed down to those under him mysteries and initiations.

14:16 Then in time, the ungodly custom became strong and was kept as law, and graven images were worshipped at the command of rulers.

14:17 And when people were not able to honor them in their presence because they lived far away, they imagined the distant appearance and made a visible image of the king they honored, so that through their eagerness they might flatter the absent one as if present.

14:18 But the ambition of the craftsman advanced even those who did not know him in worship;

14:19 for he, wishing to please the one who employed him, used his art to force the likeness to look finer,

14:20 and the crowd, attracted by the beauty of the work, now considered as an object of worship the one who a little before they had honored as a man.

14:21 And this became a hidden trap for life, because people, enslaved either to calamity or to tyranny, invested stone and wood with the incommunicable Name.

14:22 Then it was not enough for them to go astray concerning the knowledge of God, but while living in the great conflict of ignorance they call such great evils peace.

14:23 For either slaughtering children in their initiations, or celebrating secret mysteries, or holding frenzied revels of strange ordinances,

14:24 they no longer keep either their lives or their marriages pure; but one either destroys another by treachery or grieves him by adultery.

14:25 And everywhere there reigns a confusion of blood and murder, theft and deceit, corruption, faithlessness, tumult, perjury,

14:26 disturbance of good men, forgetfulness of favors, pollution of souls, inversion of sex, disorder in marriages, adultery, and licentiousness.

14:27 For the worship of idols that may not be named is the beginning and cause and end of every evil.

14:28 For they either celebrate in exaltation, or prophesy lies, or live unrighteously, or readily forswear themselves.

14:29 For because they trust in lifeless idols, when they have sworn falsely they expect not to be harmed.

14:30 But just retribution will overtake them for both reasons: because they thought wrongly about God in devoting themselves to idols, and because they swore unrighteously in deceit, despising holiness.

14:31 For it is not the power of those by whom they swear, but the just penalty for those who sin, that always follows after the transgression of the unrighteous.
